summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for fever, elevated white blood cell count, and worsening kidney function. She had a painful, infected left below-knee amputation stump with pustular exudate and warmth. Hyperkalemia (potassium 7.0) was managed with emergency treatment, and acute kidney injury was attributed to recent Bactrim use, which was discontinued. She underwent a left above-knee amputation after multidisciplinary evaluation due to non-healing infection. Bone culture grew vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus and coagulase-negative staphylococcus, prompting continued IV vancomycin therapy. Her pain was managed with a PCA pump initially, then transitioned to oral medications including gabapentin, oxycodone, and MS Contin. She completed a course of oral vancomycin for suspected C. diff. Her infection and renal function improved, and she was discharged home with home nursing for IV antibiotics, a hospital bed, and follow-up care.
